title: Fairness-Aware Test-Time Prompt Tuning
method: Vision-language soft-prompt gradients; target/spurious entropy objectives and controlled adaptation.
decision: Keep the task/sensitive-cue distinction in editing guidance. Do not import gradients, image augmentation or its guarantees into black-box textual optimization.

title: Guiding LLM Decision-Making with Fairness Reward Models
method: Train a fairness reward model on weakly annotated reasoning; aggregate multiple reasoning chains.
decision: Use error evidence and task-grounded fairness requirements. Do not add a trained judge or dozens of inference chains under an unreported budget.

title: LLM Prompt Duel Optimizer: Efficient Label-Free Prompt Optimization
method: Pairwise LLM-judge feedback, Double Thompson Sampling and top-performer mutation/pruning.
decision: Adapt measured top-parent refinement and bounded candidate generation. We already have gold labels, so use cached measured objectives; no LLM judge, dueling bandit posterior or copied PDO algorithm is claimed.

title: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Approach to Prompt Optimization in NLP
method: DQN/PPO chooses predefined edits with a weighted reward over cultural sentence pairs.
decision: Use explicit edit categories as an engineering analogy. Do not import its scalar reward, trained RL policy, or missing-bias-to-zero preprocessing; those are incompatible with measured three-objective Pareto evaluation.

title: Fairness Aware Reinforcement Learning via Proximal Policy Optimization
method: Fair-PPO penalizes retrospective/prospective reward disparities in multi-agent environments.
decision: Motivates guarding utility while reducing supported group errors. No PPO/value network or multi-agent fairness-transfer claim is implemented.

title: Rethinking Prompt Optimizers: From Prompt Merits to Optimization
method: Identifies clarity, precision, concise reasoning and preservation of original information; trains a merit-guided optimizer.
decision: Implement these merits in bounded local revision requests and preserve conditional label rules during contract cleanup. Do not claim reproduction of the trained MePO model.

title: Attention Pruning: Automated Fairness Repair of Language Models via Surrogate Simulated Annealing
method: Surrogate neural networks guide simulated annealing over attention-head pruning masks.
decision: The fixed target model must stay fixed. Do not prune its heads or train a surrogate from our small pilot and report model repair as prompt optimization.

title: Cost-Aware Model Selection for Text Classification: Multi-Objective Trade-offs Between Fine-Tuned Encoders and LLM Prompting in Production
method: Compare encoder/LLM accuracy, latency and costs with reproducible artifacts and Pareto analyses.
decision: Preserve exact inference-token accounting, backend diagnostics and source hashes. Model-family switching is a different experiment; Qwen remains fixed in this pilot.

title: Multi-Objective Scheduling for Large Language Model Inference with Prompt-Level Cost Prediction and SLO Awareness
method: Predict cost/latency and route workloads across execution pools; simulation-based carbon/SLO analysis.
decision: Use the existing exact tokenizer-based admission controller rather than a newly trained scheduler. No inferred HPC billing, carbon or task-quality improvement is imported.

title: Fairness Aware Reward Optimization
method: Train reward models under demographic parity/equalized-odds/counterfactual constraints; reward/policy theory.
decision: The useful distinction is utility preservation versus fairness repair. Our supported quality guard is a heuristic; FARO certificates and reward-to-policy transfer do not apply to these discrete prompt edits.

title: Fairness-Aware Prompt Tuning: Selective Prompt Allocation for Bias Reduction in NLP Models
method: Architectural discussion of a catalog of soft prompts and an input-dependent allocator using auxiliary/proxy features.
decision: Do not route by protected attributes or add an unaccounted prompt ensemble. Conditional prompt routing changes deployment semantics and needs its own protocol; retain one static prompt per candidate here.
